notice_details.underlying_problems: Recent water sample for November 18th, 2025 show unsatisfactory results with total coliform counts greater than 200cfu/100mL. The source of the contamination is currently unknown and unconfirmed, but it is suspected that recent changes to the water system may have introduced contamination. The main surface source water pump failed, and they switched over to a shallow well which pumps into a cistern. The alternative water source feeds into the current treatment system that includes filtration, softening, UV disinfection and chlorination. The resort itself is also going under recent renovation that started early November 2025.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: EHO has contacted and explained the situation to the operator and issued a Boil Water Notice on the water system. Operator will take responsibility to ensure all users are informed about the Boil Water Notice. Operator is currently providing bottled water to users for drinking purposes. Operator to ensure boil water notice signs are posted at all drinking water taps. EHO has provided information on how to operate food services during a BWN.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: 1) Repair the water system and have it functioning accordingly to its approved design. 2) Disinfect the water system and flush accordingly. Follow manufacture's instructions for the different system components to ensure they do not get damaged. 3) Greater than 7 days after disinfection, submit two sets of bacteriological water samples showing the absence of total coliforms and E.coli. Each set of samples must be taken at least 24 hours apart. 4) Contact the local Environmental Health Officer to review the file and rescind the boil water notice if applicable.

name: Dease Lake Air Tanker Base Water System (building #72116)
facility_name: Dease Lake Air Tanker Base Water System (building #72116)

notice_details.underlying_problems: A sample of the treated water was taken on January 27, 2026 for general chemical analysis which led to a determination that the guideline limit for arsenic (0.01 mg/L) had been exceeded – result was 0.0650 mg/L. The source for this water system is a deep well (WTN 49208) which draws from an aquifer that has naturally high arsenic. A treatment system has been installed and includes a component for lowering arsenic to below to guideline limit. It appears this treatment system component requires maintenance (i.e., media replacement). Other treatment system components also appear to require maintenance as the system for lowering hardness appears to be non-functinal, and the system for lowering manganese appears to be only partially effective. This water system is mostly used seasonally from May to October and only one of two connected buildings are in use at this time. As a precaution for maintenance and custodial staff who may infrequently use the connected building, the operator has posted Do Not Consume notices at points where drinking water can be obtained. This notice will remain in effect until additional testing can be done, the treatment system is repaired and/or maintained to ensure it’s performing as designed, performance of the treatment system is verified through additional testing, a trained operator is in place, and written operations & maintenance procedures are available for the operator.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: Per the plan detailed under corrective actions.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: 1) Submit a follow-up sample of treated water for general chemical analysis to verify the treatment system is non-funtional. 2) Based on results of the follow-up sample, take whatever corrective actions are required to repair and/or maintain treatment system components. 3) After repairs and/or maintenance is complete, submit a sample to determine if the treatment system is performing as designed. 4) Provide an operator who is capable of operating & maintaining the treatment system and other components of the water system. 5) Provide a written set of procedures which details how each treatment system and water system component is to be operated & maintained.

When no monitoring for total coliform bacteria or Escherichia coli is performed, it is not possible to demonstrate that the water is potable and that contamination by bacteria has not occurred.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: On Jul 9, 2025: Environmental Health Officer issued advisory to the water supplier instructing them to issue a Water Quality Advisory – boil water before consumption. See Corrective Actions Remaining and Underlying Problems for more information.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: On Jul 9, 2025: Owners of public premises served by this water system must: (a) notify the public that a water quality advisory by posting a sign at every sink or drinking water fountain accessible to the public; (b) if normal business practices provide an opportunity, verbally advise any person who may use the domestic water system for a domestic purpose that the a boil water notice is in effect. (c) boil water before consumption (d) the water supplier must submit two sets of water samples from the water system to an approved laboratory for microbiological testing. The two sets of samples will need to be collected at least 24 hours apart. Satisfactory results (i.e. results that show no detectable total coliform bacteria or Escherichia coli present) will need to be received. (e) the water supplier must submit a raw water sample to a laboratory for chemical analysis and provide the report to the Environmental Health Officer. (f) the water supplier to arrange a person certified with small water system operator training to oversee the water system. (g) the water supplier to provide an emergency response plan which must be satisfied by the Environmental Health Officer.

notice_details.underlying_problems: Treatment plant has been upgraded and preliminary test results show effective reduction of manganese, iron, and hardness. Further testing will be required to ensure manganese levels are maintained below the maximum acceptable concentration of 0.12mg/L. Sodium levels are elevated significantly higher than the aesthetic objective. The aesthetic objective for sodium in drinking water is ≤200 mg/L. The taste of drinking water is generally considered offensive at sodium concentrations above the aesthetic objective. Sodium is not considered a toxic element; up to 5 g/day of sodium is consumed by normal adults. Although the average intake of sodium from drinking water is only a small fraction of that consumed in a normal diet, the intake from this source could be significant for persons suffering from hypertension or congestive heart failure who may require a sodium-restricted diet.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: Treatment plant upgraded this year to address several chemical/physical parameters of concern. Bacteriological and chemical/physical test restuls have been acceptable with the exception of sodium, which is above the AO of 200mg/L. Do Not Consume notice rescinded. Water Quality Advisory notice distributed to residents. Separate drinking water supply is available to the residents.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: A full panel of chemical/physical tests within the next month with satisfactory restuls will be required, followed by testing of manganese and other parameters of concern at an enhanced frequency to ensure continued treatment efficacy. Regular notification to residents of the elevated sodium concentration including the following: Sodium in drinking water is not a health concern for most people but may be an issue for someone with severe hypertension, congestive heart failure or on a sodium-restricted diet. Further, it is recommended that water from a water softener not be given to infants and not be used in the preparation of infant beverages including formula and juice. Water softeners may increase the levels of sodium in drinking water.

name: Granisle CWS

notice_details.underlying_problems: Coagulant from treatment is leaking into the distribution system as reported by water system users. Testing of treated water showed aluminum from coagulant in excess of the maximum acceptable concentration (MAC). The concentration of the raw water was below the operational guidance level so the aluminum is coming from the treatment. Raw water was 0.0255 mg/L and the treated water is 3.75 mg/L. MAC is 2.9 mg/L Turbidity of the treated water was also elevated and above the 1 NTU required for treated surface water. Treated water was 2.72 NTU. Babies, young children, pregnant women, breastfeeding mothers and individuals with kidney complications or on dialysis are at a higher risk of health effects from elevated aluminum. Water system currently on a Water Quality Advisory (WQA) due to operational deficiencies. Underlying problems of the WQA are: 1) One of two Ceramic Ultrafiltration unit (CUF- B) was turned off due to a structural defect. 2) The second CUF unit - A, which serves as the primary treatment barrier for the removal of inorganic and organic constituents, as well as protozoan pathogens such as Giardia and Cryptosporidium, did not meet the requirements of the Indirect Integrity test as stipulated in the permit conditions. 3) The turbidity sensor shut off on the SCADA system used for conducting the Indirect Integrity test is disabled. Turbidity levels in the treated water were observed to exceed 1.06 NTU. 4) The lack of Indirect Integrity Testing, combined with elevated turbidity readings in the treated water, may be indicative of treatment system malfunction
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: Water system owner will notify the residents of the community about the change from the WQA to a Do Not Consume notice Communication will highlight the vulnerable members of the community Water system owners will provide an alternative drinking water source for those in the community affected by the notice. Northern Health will post the notice on their public drinking water notice page to assist with awareness
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: Test various locations in the distribution system to see if the elevated aluminum and turbidity is consistent throughout the distribution system. Test the output of both CUF units during operation to determine if one or both are leaking coagulant. Have a professional audit the treatment system to find out the source of coagulant leakage. Apply corrective measures to ensure the aluminum operational guideline of 0.1 mg/L is consistently met in the treated water going forward. Perform a visual inspection of the wet well and storage tower looking for coagulant settling on the bottom. Seek out professional advice on cleaning out the coagulant from the distribution system lines. When sample results show a decrease in aluminum in the distribution and the concentration is below the MAC, the Do Not Consume Notice (DNC) can be rescinded and replaced with a Water Quality Advisory. The Water Quality Advisory will retain the non-completed requirements from the DNC (except aluminum above the MAC) and remain in place until the test results show the aluminum is below the operational guidance of 0.1 mg/L Existing requirements of the previous Water Quality will remain as requirements and be added to the DNC but will not need to be met for rescinding the DNC. Those requirements are as follows: 1) Conduct a comprehensive assessment of CUF A in collaboration with the manufacturer or a qualified professional to identify the root cause of the current operational concerns and ensure that the operational malfunctions are addressed such that the CUF unit is working as designed and approved. 2) Operator to identify the cause of elevated levels of turbidity in the treated water. 3) Permeate turbidity levels rgfgthe CUF A must be continuously within the range outlined on the operating permit. Indirect Integrity Testing must be operational, with alarm and shutdown points enabled. 4) Conduct Direct Integrity Testing (DIT) for the CUF A daily and ensure that the results are documented. Provide the results of the DIT to the Environmental Health Officer on a weekly basis for a review.

Operator was directed to adjust the chlorine injector to ensure that 0.2ppm FAC residual was maintained throughout the distribution at all times. No additional water treatment is required at this time. Well and reservoir has been chlorine shocked according to the operator.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: 1. Disinfect the well, distribution system and reservoir. 2. Additional treatment may be required, subject to inspection findings and the degree of surface water influence. 3. It is required that the results of 2 consecutive water samples from the Gulbrandser and John Hamblin’s House sampling locations, taken a minimum of 24 hours apart, are absent for Total Coliform and E. coli. These results must be submitted to the Northern Health before the removal of the Boil Water Notice will be considered.

notice_details.underlying_problems: Manganese levels exceed the Canadian Drinking Water Quality Guidelines maximum allowable concentration (MAC) of 0.12mg/L. Manganese is a naturally occurring element found in food, soil, air and in drinking water. It is a necessary mineral for human health, however based on recent research, developmental impairment has been shown in bottle fed infants and young children if there is too high of Manganese ingestion through contaminated drinking water. An assessment of manganese levels was conducted in 2021, 2022 and 2023 by sampling the water. Upon completion, it was determined that manganese levels exceeded the MAC of 0.12mg/L and, as a result, a community advisory would be required. A health advisory is in now in effect for bottle fed infants.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: Notify impacted users of the Water Quality Advisory (WQA) as per the steps outlined during a recent inspection. Signage to be posted in view of the users at the pumphouse and monitored to ensure they remain in place throughout the advisory. Continue to monitor level of manganese and report results to EHO.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: Consideration of treatment plant options to lower source manganese levels below 0.12mg/L as per the Canadian Drinking Water Quality Guidelines. Send results to EHO indicating the level of manganese is below the MAC.

notice_details.underlying_problems: Exceedance of the Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality Maximum Acceptable Concentration (MAC) for Antimony of >0.006mg/L were identified in the water sample sites that are reportable under the Drinking Water Protection Act in 2015, 2016, 2017, 2018, 2021, & 2022. Northern Health was advised of the exceedances in April 2025 and is now formally addressing the exceedance. Antimony is a naturally occurring chemical that can also find its way into a water supply system from industrial effluents or leaching from plumbing materials & solder. The rational for implementing a Do not consume advisory is that the risk with antimony in drinking water is seen through consumption of the water which may result in adverse effects to the liver and GI system etc. Antimony does not enter the body through the skin or through the lungs via vapor making the water still acceptable for use in sanitation purposes.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: Initiated Emergency Response Plan (2021) Notified all users that a Do not consume advisory is in effect (2021) Placed appropriate “non-potable” signs above each tap. (2021) Provided potable bottled water to users (since 2021) Northern Health (NH) has a provided a letter to Red Chris addressing the responsibility of a water supply operator that under the Drinking Water Protection Act & Regulation they must advise Northern Health of any chemical exceedances as soon as possible.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: Upgrade water treatment to maintain Antimony Levels below the Canadian Drinking Water Quality Guidelines Maximum Allowable Concentration of 0.006mg/L. Response from Red Chris regarding the letter provided by NH

name: Kitimat Community Water System
facility_location: East of Kitimat River near Highway Bridge, Kitimat

notice_details.underlying_problems: The Kitimat water system draws water from the Kitimat River via two infiltration galleries which provide partial filtration for turbidity; however, as the water level in the river rises the effectiveness of the filtration goes down. Historically, at a water level of 1.8 m the turbidity of water post infiltration goes over 1 NTU which reduces the effectiveness of chlorine disinfection and makes it difficult to maintain a minimum residual of 0.2 ppm free chlorine throughout the distribution system. Snow melt has lead to an increased water level in the river and higher turbidity post infiltration (1.17 NTU). While the water supplier stored clean water when the river level was < 1.8 m, reservoir levels were at the point where dirty water needed to be pumped into the system on the night of May 6 2026 to ensure a sufficient volume is available for fire protection. The turbidity in the system is still >1 NTU as of the morning of May 7 2026. However, the water level has dropped since then and the advisory is expected to remain in place until tomorrow afternoon dependent on turbidity results. The underlying problem for this water system is that there is inadequate treatment of water from the surface water source.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: Pump only as much high turbidity water as is necessary into the system and verify a minimum of 0.2 ppm free chlorine can be maintained. If free chlorine cannot be maintained above 0.2 ppm throughout the distribution system or if the water post infiltration goes over 5 NTU, this WQA will likely be upgraded to a Boil Water Notice.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: Flush dirty water from the system and maintain a minimum 0.2 ppm free chlorine residual and establish a turbidity level of < 1 NTU throughout the distribution system.

notice_details.underlying_problems: Chemical sampling history shows consistent manganese concentrations above the MAC in 5 of the 6 wells. Manganese has long been considered an aesthetic concern in drinking water (e.g. causing stains on laundry, plumbing fixtures, etc.). However, new scientific studies show potential health effects from long term exposure to high levels of manganese in drinking water. This new information was used to revise the guideline for manganese in drinking water.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: Information packages containing information on manganese in drinking water have been distributed by the operator to the residents.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: 1. Distribute updated notice and information to residents 2. Continue additional sampling to determine the level of manganese in the distribution system. Collect samples from multiple points throughout the distribution system and submit to an accredited lab for manganese testing. Provide sample results to Northern Health. 3. Continue talks with a qualified drinking water professional to assess the water source and propose a suitable treatment system to reduce the level of manganese to below the Maximum Acceptable Concentration. 4. Submit the treatment proposal to Northern Health in the form of a Construction Permit application. 5. Upon receipt of approval from a Northern Health Public Health Engineer, in the form of a Construction Permit, install the approved treatment system. 6. Conduct post-treatment samples in accordance with the conditions of the Construction Permit to verify treatment efficacy.

notice_details.underlying_problems: Chemical/physical sampling history shows variations in manganese concentrations from the source and within the distribution system with some samples exceeding the Maximum Acceptable Concentration (MAC). Manganese has long been considered only an aesthetic concern in drinking water (e.g. causing stains on laundry, plumbing fixtures, etc.). However, new scientific studies show potential health effects from exposure to long term exposure to high levels of manganese in drinking water. This new information was used to revise the guideline for manganese in drinking water in 2019. Health Canada has set the Maximum Acceptable Concentration (MAC) of 0.12 mg/L (120µg/L) for manganese in drinking water. The MAC is intended to protect all Canadians, but is based on the most vulnerable/sensitive population (e.g. infants and young children). If drinking water exceeds the MAC for manganese, another source of water, such as bottled water, should be used for preparing baby formula for infants and young children. Adults who drink water with manganese levels above the MAC are at lower risk than infants and children, but may wish to consider other sources of drinking water or home treatment systems.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: The Town of Smithers is currently investigating treatment options to reduce the levels of manganese. Information related to the advisory has been delivered door-to-door to impacted residents on July 06, 2023. Chemical sampling (post treatment) should continue to be conducted annually but the Town of Smithers may consider more enhanced sampling to enhance understanding of manganese exposure events. The "Guidelines for Canadian Drinking Water Quality: Guideline Technical Document – Manganese" should be consulted to determine best practices.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: Provide a plan of action to the Health Authority by October 01, 2023. It is recommended that utilities develop a distribution system management plan to minimize the likelihood of manganese release events in the distribution system. Plan created should include approximate timelines for when actions identified would be taken. A treatment plant is being proposed and hopes to be installed sometime in the spring of 2024. Information related to the advisory to be included within the Annual Report and distributed to users annually.

notice_details.underlying_problems: System is a shallow well with no treatment. Error in sampling or error in annual routine shock chlorination are currently the suspected causes for contamination. August 18, 2025 - Operator had completed 2 shock treatment but was not able to remove contamiation. There are 3 unstantisfoactory results prior to the business closing for the season. Inspection completed on-site and the shallow well was not protected from contamination. Bugs can be found floating on the surface of the well.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: June 19, 2023 - Operator has been contacted via phone. The operator was made aware of the adverse sample results and was interviewed to determine potential causes of contamination. The operator asked to resample the next day. An email was provided to summarize the required actions and 1 set of sample requisition forms has been provided. Operator notified Dianna Vuu that they instead shock chlorinated the water system overnight. June 20, 2023 - A risk assessment was been conducted by Dianna Vuu in consultation with TL Allison Crowe. As a new accurate sample will not be available until one week after the shock chlorination, a BWN will be issued as a precaution. Operator has been provided another email outlining the new required corrective actions for the issued BWN. Operator has been provided another set of sample requisition forms. June 21, 2023 - Operator confirmed that the water users have been notified of the BWN. Signage has been posted. June 28, 2023 - Operator has confirmed that a sample was submitted on June 27, 2023 (one week ater the date of shock chlorination. June 30, 2023 - The first satisfactory sample set has been received. November 14, 2025 - Chat with operator (Melcor) on requirements to lifting the BWN.
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: The boil water notice may be lifted once the above actions are completed and Northern Health has received 2 consecutive satisfactory samples that were collected at least 24 hours apart.

notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: - Collect bacteriological samples using proper sampling technique, including faucet disinfection. - Submit two bacteriological water samples showing the absence of total coliforms and E.coli. notice_details.underlying_problems: Talking with the operator, it sounds like there had been a bout of heavy rain and there was little to no chlorine within the water system. Given that the well is heavily influenced by surface water, combined with the fact there was no chlorine in the system, I think that these circumstances came together to result in the unsatisfactory water quality results we saw from June 21st. This water system needs treatment and is required to have treatment works installed by October 3, 2016. Until then, a longer term BWN needs to be considered… thoughts for further discussion.
notice_details.steps_taken_to_remedy: Tatuk Lake Resort was put on a boil water notice due to unsatisfactory water quality results at 4 of 5 sampling locations. See below: Residence – TC = 21, E.coli = L1 Campsite Standpipe – TC = 29, E.coli = L1 Cabin 1 – TC = EST 25, E.coli = EST 1 Showerhouse – TC = 18, E.coli = L1
notice_details.corrective_actions_remaining: Operator needs to post signage at all taps indicating that there is a boil water notice, notify current guests, and inform all new guests on arrival. Operator was also asked to shock chlorinate and flush the system. Operator is required to submit two samples 24 hours apart with satisfactory results prior to the BWN being lifted. Chlorine was also discussed with the operator. It was instructed that chlorine needs to be added to the system in such a way that there is a uniform distribution of chlorine throughout the water system at all times.
